ai.definition: A quantum gravity theory is an attempt to unify general relativity with quantum mechanics, providing a framework that could explain how gravity works on the smallest scales.
ai.howItWorks: Theories in this field propose new mathematical models and frameworks to describe gravitational phenomena at the quantum scale, potentially leading to a unified description of all fundamental forces.
ai.problemSolved: Current theories cannot reconcile general relativity with quantum mechanics, which is necessary for a complete understanding of the universe's fundamental interactions.
ai.buildProcess: Theoretical development and mathematical modeling; no direct manufacturing process as it is primarily theoretical research.
ai.costDrivers: High due to advanced computational resources and theoretical expertise required; funding from academic institutions or government agencies.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Long-term theoretical exploration with potential for breakthroughs in fundamental physics, but no immediate practical applications.
ai.risks: Theoretical uncertainties and lack of experimental evidence; high risk due to the speculative nature of the field.
ai.profitability: Not applicable as a theory; potential long-term benefits for scientific understanding and technology development if successful.
ai.futureDevelopment: Continued theoretical exploration, possibly with advancements in computational power and experimental techniques that could test predictions.

glossary.def: A theory of gravitation formulated by Albert Einstein, describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
A fundamental theory in physics that describes nature at the smallest scales of energy levels of atoms and subatomic particles.
A theoretical structure that combines different physical theories into a single, coherent description. In this context, it refers to merging general relativity with quantum mechanics.

subsystems.name: Mathematical framework
subsystems.role: a self-consistent quantum theory whose low-energy limit is general relativity.
parts: quantum field theory on curved spacetime
candidate frameworks: string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety, causal sets

subsystems.name: Correspondence checks
subsystems.role: prove the candidate theory reproduces the physics already measured.
parts: classical limit to Einstein's field equations
recovery of Standard Model matter and forces

subsystems.name: Phenomenology
subsystems.role: turn abstract mathematics into a number an experiment could look for.
parts: modified dispersion relations for light and particles

subsystems.name: Precision laboratory experiments
subsystems.role: test gravity's behaviour at short range and in the quantum regime.
parts: torsion balances and short-range gravity tests
quantum-limited readout and shielding from vibration

subsystems.name: Astrophysical observatories
subsystems.role: use the universe as the high-energy laboratory nobody can build on Earth.

subsystems.name: Quantum simulation
subsystems.role: mimic candidate behaviour in controllable laboratory systems.
parts: analogue horizons in fluids or optics

buildSteps.title: Choose the starting assumption
buildSteps.detail: Either quantise the geometry of spacetime itself, or treat gravity as an emergent, collective effect of other quantum degrees of freedom.

buildSteps.title: Construct the formalism
buildSteps.detail: Write down a mathematical structure that is finite and self-consistent at the Planck scale, where ordinary quantum field theory breaks down.

buildSteps.title: Check the known limits
buildSteps.detail: Show the theory reduces to general relativity at large distances and to quantum field theory at ordinary energies — otherwise it is dead on arrival.

buildSteps.title: Derive one observable
buildSteps.detail: Find an effect that is not exactly zero, even if it is suppressed by the Planck scale of about 10^19 GeV, and calculate its size.

buildSteps.title: Sharpen the measurement
buildSteps.detail: Improve sensors — quantum-limited interferometry, atom interferometers, torsion balances — until they can reach the predicted size.

buildSteps.title: Run tabletop and short-range tests
buildSteps.detail: Look for deviations from Newtonian gravity below a millimetre and for gravity-induced entanglement between two small masses.

buildSteps.title: Mine astrophysical data
buildSteps.detail: Search gravitational-wave and cosmic microwave background records for energy-dependent travel times, extra polarisation or missing high-energy particles.

buildSteps.title: Confront with data and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Every null result kills whole families of models, narrowing the space until one framework survives every test.

prerequisites.why: the working language of particle physics, and the thing that must be reconciled with gravity.
the tested classical description of gravity that any quantum version must reproduce.
merging black holes probe strong, rapidly changing gravity unavailable in any laboratory.
testing Planck-suppressed effects needs sensing at or beyond today's noise floors.
the relevant energy is about 10^15 times larger than the most powerful colliders reach, so evidence must come indirectly.

pathway.milestone: competing frameworks developed and laboratory limits on short-range deviations from Newtonian gravity tightened
pathway.unlocks: a clear map of which ideas are already ruled out.

pathway.milestone: tabletop tests of whether gravity can entangle two masses
pathway.unlocks: the first direct evidence that gravity has quantum behaviour.

pathway.milestone: next-generation gravitational-wave and cosmic microwave background surveys
pathway.unlocks: high-precision probes of light propagation and polarisation across cosmic distances.

pathway.milestone: a framework that makes one confirmed, non-gravitational prediction
pathway.unlocks: a real theory of quantum gravity rather than a family of candidates.
